title: Matt Pocock on TypeScript mental models, open objects, TS expect error vs as any, and becoming an educator
summary: Matt explains TypeScript as a shorter feedback loop in your IDE, why its open object types surprise people, and why a targeted as any beats TS ignore or TS expect error. He also argues complex types usually come from complex JavaScript and favors JSDoc plus handwritten docs.

principles.text: TypeScript is mainly a shorter feedback loop in your IDE, so you can code longer before checking in the browser.
principles.quote: in TypeScript you have a shorter feedback loop, which is you have the feedback loop inside your IDE.

principles.text: TypeScript object types are open: excess properties are allowed unless the object is a fresh literal, so don't assume keys are exact.
principles.quote: TypeScript has open objects, whereas Flow Flow would actually error there.

principles.text: Complex types usually mean complex JavaScript; simplify the code and its abstractions before reaching for harder types.
principles.quote: complex TypeScript comes from complex JavaScript, cuz TypeScript is just an effort to describe JavaScript.

principles.text: Avoid chaining derived types across boundaries; decoupled types let each part change independently.
principles.quote: They end up creating these chains of linked types linked through generic functions they're not even really aware of that end up making the system really coupled.

principles.text: TS ignore and TS expect error are sledgehammers hitting the whole next line; prefer a targeted as any on the specific node.
principles.quote: as any targets a specific node, a specific thing. It's not destroying the entire next line.

principles.text: Write rich JSDoc comments on APIs and pair them with handwritten docs rather than relying on auto-generated doc sites.
principles.quote: tons and tons of jsdoc comments of real high quality explaining all of the stuff uh of what your API should do and then a really nicely written documentation site to kind of match that up
